data.narrative:
Q-CTRL, a Series B quantum computing software company that has raised $132M to date, sits within a sector comprising 3 public and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, and D-Wave Quantum. The quantum computing landscape remains sufficiently immature and heterogeneous that direct peer multiples offer limited statistical reliability.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised ($132M) as a baseline value proxy and applying a typical Series B-to-Series C step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $251M. This method assumes Q-CTRL's prior rounds were priced at or near fair value and that sector-standard expansion multiples apply. The range around this central estimate spans $213M (low, applying a 1.6x multiplier) to $288M (high, applying a 2.2x multiplier), reflecting uncertainty in the appropriate step-up coefficient for an early-stage quantum software business.

A peer-median cross-check cannot be performed: while five quantum computing companies exist in the comparable universe, none yielded sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints to support robust statistical inference. The triangulated valuation range of $213M–$288M (median $251M) relies on a single method and should be stress-tested against deployment metrics, customer concentration, and pathway to enterprise adoption as additional diligence proceeds.
